---
title: AI and agents
description: Point a coding agent at the files that teach it ClipMux, from a one-line prompt to every page as Markdown.
icon: Bot
---

A coding agent can add ClipMux to your app if it reads the right file first.
These docs publish one written for that job, plus every page as Markdown and
the API as an OpenAPI spec, so the agent works from the same facts you do
instead of guessing.

## Start with one prompt

Paste this into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any agent that can fetch a URL,
from your app's project:

```txt
Read https://clipmux.com/agents.md, then add ClipMux uploads, webhooks and signed playback to this app.
```

`https://clipmux.com/agents.md` is the onboarding guide for agents. It
gives the rules (no secret in browser code, no hand-rolled HMAC or JWT code,
access decided in your own callbacks), the steps from
`npx @clipmux/node init` to `doctor`, and a table of error codes with their
fixes. It also links to the docs index, the Build docs in full,
Troubleshooting and the OpenAPI spec.

The guide's body is the `AGENTS.md` that ships inside the `@clipmux/node`
package, so an agent that has already installed the SDK finds the same text
at `node_modules/@clipmux/node/AGENTS.md`, matching the installed version.

`init` asks the ClipMux server's owner to approve the app in the
dashboard, so the agent will ask you to open an approval link. It writes
the credentials to `.env.local` without printing them, and the guide tells
the agent never to print or log them either.

## The docs as Markdown

| URL | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `https://clipmux.com/llms.txt` | The index, in the llms.txt format: every page's title, its one-line description and a link to its Markdown. |
| `https://clipmux.com/llms-full.txt` | Every page in one file. |
| `https://clipmux.com/docs/build/llms-full.txt` | The Build tab in one file: integrating an app. |
| `https://clipmux.com/docs/self-host/llms-full.txt` | The Self-host tab in one file: installing and running a server. |
| `https://clipmux.com/docs/reference/llms-full.txt` | The Reference tab: the API, webhooks, errors, limits, settings and CLI. |
| `https://clipmux.com/docs/resources/llms-full.txt` | The Resources tab: migrating, the architecture, the FAQ. |

Every page is also served as Markdown at its own URL plus `.md`. This page,
for example, is at `https://clipmux.com/docs/build/ai-and-agents.md`, and the
introduction at `https://clipmux.com/docs.md`.

For an agent with a small context, point it at the tab it needs rather than
`llms-full.txt`: an app integration needs only the Build tab.

## Page actions

Each page has two buttons under its title and description:

- **Copy page** copies the page's Markdown, to paste into any chat.
- **Open in** opens the page's Markdown (**View as Markdown**), starts a chat
  in **Claude**, **ChatGPT** or **Cursor** that is told to read the page and
  help you with ClipMux, or opens the page's source on GitHub
  (**Edit on GitHub**).

<LeavesYourServers>
  Open in Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor sends that service a prompt naming the
  page's public URL, and nothing else. What you then type into the chat goes
  to that service under its own terms.
</LeavesYourServers>

## The OpenAPI spec

The integration API, the delivery URLs and the webhooks are described as
OpenAPI 3.1 at `https://clipmux.com/openapi.json`. Every ClipMux server
also serves its own copy at `GET /openapi.json`, with no credential, so an
agent can read the spec of the exact version you run:

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/openapi.json | jq '.info.version, (.paths | keys)'
```

Use it to generate a client in another language, or to let an agent check
a request before it sends one. The routes the dashboard uses with the
owner's session are not in it; see the
[Management API](/docs/reference/management-api).

## Check it works

Ask the agent to run, once it has finished:

```bash
npx @clipmux/node doctor
```

It must end with `✓ Ready.` If it doesn't, each line names the credential or
setting that failed. Then upload a test file:

```bash
npx @clipmux/node upload sample.mp4 --passthrough lesson_42 --wait
```
